sections.title: Level 3 Advanced Strategy
sections.content: At Level 3, questions are not based directly on raw data but on derived values, abstract variables, and equations. Step 1: Carefully read the chart and identify all variables. Step 2: Derive quantities (profit, ratio, growth) from the given data. Step 3: Map abstract variables (A, B, C) to real values. Step 4: Form secondary equations. Step 5: Logically verify the final answer.

sections.title: Derived Commercial Data
sections.content: Step 1: Extract data such as sales, cost, and revenue from the chart. Step 2: Apply required formulas (Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price). Step 3: Calculate percentage or ratio. Step 4: Perform comparison. Example: If SP = 120 and CP = 100, then profit = 20 and profit% = 20%.

sections.title: Abstract Variables Interpretation
sections.content: Step 1: Map variables like A, B, C to categories. Step 2: Extract each variable’s value from the chart. Step 3: Form relationships (A > B, A + B = C). Step 4: Draw logical conclusions.

sections.title: Forming Secondary Equations
sections.content: Step 1: Create equations from primary data. Step 2: Build secondary equations for unknown values. Step 3: Solve simultaneously. Step 4: Check whether all conditions are satisfied.

sections.title: Multi-Step Comparison
sections.content: Step 1: Extract values of multiple variables. Step 2: Compute derived data (percentage, ratio). Step 3: Apply conditions. Step 4: Perform final comparison. Step 5: Choose the correct option.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Treating direct values as final answers. 2. Applying incorrect formulas for derived values. 3. Errors in variable mapping. 4. Missing data while forming equations. 5. Not verifying the final answer.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: At Level 3, Radar/Web DI is based on advanced logic. Correct use of derived values, abstract variables, and equations is essential to reach the right answer. A step-wise approach and verification are very important.

tricks.title: Derived Value Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Use formulas to calculate required values instead of relying on direct data.

tricks.title: Variable Mapping Trick
tricks.explanation: Quickly link A, B, C to chart categories.
tricks.example: A = Sales, B = Cost, C = Profit.

tricks.title: Equation Formation Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Form equations using totals or relationships.

tricks.title: Ratio Conversion Trick
tricks.explanation: Convert percentages into ratios for easier comparison.

tricks.title: Step-wise Filtering
tricks.explanation: Apply each condition one by one.
tricks.example: First check A > B, then A + C.

tricks.title: Approximation Use
tricks.explanation: Round complex numbers to simplify calculations.

tricks.title: Cross Check Method
tricks.explanation: Verify the final answer by substituting it into all equations.
tricks.example: The obtained value should satisfy the equation.

tricks.title: Elimination Technique
tricks.explanation: Remove incorrect options to reach the correct answer.
tricks.example: Eliminate values that do not satisfy the conditions.
